0.content:
AVERETH
The known world is dominated by one immense continent, Avereth, surrounded by ocean. Civilizations, species, religions and dynasties have risen and vanished over immense history; some ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as myth.

Tone is high fantasy with contrast: safe cities, trade, families and festivals coexist with dangerous wilderness, Dungeons, political violence and old powers. The setting is not uniformly grim.

Current campaign scope defines six human kingdoms, two monster realms, the neutral Adventurers' Guild and independent high-rank actors. More great powers may exist but remain undefined until play needs them.
Human and monster states are not unified blocs and may trade, ally, feud or fight across species lines.

Material baseline: Western-fantasy medieval society alongside mana and high magic; modern/industrial technology is not assumed.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

1.content:
PUBLIC POWER KNOWLEDGE
Ordinary society broadly understands Level, Rank, Class, Skills, Skill Proficiency and Evolution.
Exact Levels require measurement (commonly Guild/temple methods); exact Core Stat numbers are not normally visible.

Most humans receive a Base Class around adulthood. Class reflects affinity rather than an absolute Skill prohibition.
Rank corresponds socially to Evolution stage: F Base, E first evolution, D second, C third, B Half-Divine, A higher Transcendent, S Full-Divine.
Standard evolution concepts are known; rare conditions are valuable secrets often held by powerful families, temples or institutions.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

2.content:
MANA / LEARNING
Mana is a normal part of Avereth and can support minor everyday uses as well as combat magic.
Ordinary formal Skills are most commonly learned from teachers or Skill Stones; experimentation alone is not the normal path for most people.

Schools and specialist academies exist. Nobles, wealthy families, militaries, temples, Adventurer families and scholarship students have better access to elite training.
Avereth does not normally use cultivation-style Sects; great houses, royal lines, temples, military lineages and old magical families fill similar institutional niches and often guard teachers, Skill Stones, rare Evolution knowledge, Gear and records.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

3.content:
EVOLUTION / LIFESPAN
Evolution improves health and longevity as well as power. Broad natural lifespans:
F ~100-120y; E ~150-180y; D ~250-350y; C ~500-700y; B ~2,000-3,000y; A ~10,000-20,000y; S 100,000y+.
These are tendencies, not protection from violence or exceptional causes.

SOCIAL POWER
Most people remain F/E. D-ranks are respected specialists/local elites; C-ranks are major regional figures; B-ranks often occupy senior institutional roles. A-ranks are rare strategic figures; S-ranks are kingdom-level deterrents.
Wealth strongly affects training access below the highest ranks, but cannot indefinitely substitute for personal power.
Exact high-rank populations are uncertain because independents and hidden individuals exist.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

4.content:
ADVENTURERS' GUILD
A neutral transnational Guild operates across recognized human kingdoms and has limited formal contact with monster realms.
It handles registration, Level/Rank certification, quests, monster/Dungeon information, rewards, material brokerage, frontier support and high-rank mediation.
Its strength is network, legitimacy, information and economic reach; it does not casually command every powerful Adventurer.

JURISDICTION BOUNDARY
The Guild does NOT replace local rulers, civil authorities, courts, town/city guards, militaries, property law or ordinary criminal law.
Its authority comes from contracts, certification, information networks, negotiated privileges and the willingness of states/communities to recognize its functions.
Local law and Guild rules may overlap, cooperate or conflict depending on established circumstances.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

5.content:
MONSTER ECOLOGY / FAUNA
On Avereth, native non-sapient fauna are part of the Monster ecology.
A wolf, deer, horse, boar, bear, bird or other familiar animal-shaped creature is mechanically a Monster with Level and Rank even when peaceful, domesticated or ecologically ordinary.
"Animal" remains normal everyday language for body type/ecology; it does not indicate a separate non-Monster rules category.

Monster classification is mechanical/ecological, NOT a synonym for hostility.
Ordinary domesticated F-rank fauna may fill the same everyday roles as livestock, mounts, hunting animals and pets where appropriate.

Monsters are natural populations, not temporary game spawns.
They reproduce, compete, migrate, establish territories/social structures, are hunted or domesticated, and may evolve through Ranks.
Most ordinary fauna around settled regions are F-rank. Higher-Rank evolved specimens become progressively rarer and more dangerous.

Sapience is separate from Monster classification.
Many Monsters are non-sapient fauna; others can speak, organize societies, rule territory and conduct diplomacy.

Elite = an explicitly exceptional individual/encounter type.
Boss = a practical label for an exceptional Dungeon-centered or encounter-defining threat, not necessarily a separate species.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

6.content:
CURRENT GREAT-POWER MAP
Human kingdoms: Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion, Duskreach.
Monster realms: Ashen Scale Dominion, Verdant Fang Court.
Additional states may exist; borders, minor states, cities, noble holdings and most history stay open until needed.

There is no permanent human-vs-monster bloc. Trade, rivalry, border conflict, non-aggression and temporary alliances all occur.

HIGH-RANK DETERRENCE
S-ranks are strategic actors, not routine battlefield units. Direct clashes risk catastrophic collateral damage and escalation, so they usually act through deterrence, diplomacy, representatives or only truly strategic intervention.
B/A-ranks handle much of the practical high-level conflict. A powerful ruler does not intervene merely because an unrelated lower-rank member of the same species/faction was killed.

7.content:
VALEDORN CROWN

Position: central Avereth.
Capital: Crownheart.
Status: strongest human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 3.

Identity:
Valedorn is the political center of human diplomacy and hosts the most influential royal court on the continent.
It possesses deep noble lineages, wealthy academies, old military institutions, and one of the largest Adventurers' Guild headquarters.

Its strength comes less from a single specialty than from having almost everything at a high level: wealth, population, military organization, magic, diplomacy, and several Full-Divine protectors.

Valedorn is powerful but not automatically dominant over every neighbor; coalitions of other kingdoms can still constrain it.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

8.content:
CAELRETH

Position: western Avereth.
Capital: Asterhall.
Status: top-tier human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
Caelreth is the continent's most academically arcane human kingdom.
It is known for magical colleges, Skill-Stone study, enchantment research, ritual theory, and old mage families.

Caelreth's nobles heavily protect rare Evolution knowledge.
Its cities contain unusually dense populations of professional mages and high-rank researchers.

Relations with the Verdant Fang Court are cautious but often scholarly and commercial rather than purely hostile.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

9.content:
VEYRHOLD

Position: eastern Avereth.
Capital: Ironward.
Status: top-tier martial kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
Veyrhold is a heavily militarized frontier kingdom shaped by centuries of dangerous borders.
Martial training, disciplined officer corps, fortified cities, and monster-hunting traditions are central to its culture.

It has the most openly tense relationship with the Ashen Scale Dominion.
Border clashes occur, but both sides avoid escalation that could draw their S-ranks into direct war.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

10.content:
SOLMERE

Position: southern coast.
Capital: Goldharbor.
Status: major kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 1.

Identity:
Solmere is Avereth's largest maritime trade power.
Ports, shipyards, merchant houses, mercenary contracts, Dungeon imports, and inter-kingdom commerce dominate its politics.

It is less militarily imposing than Valedorn or Veyrhold but can buy expertise, logistics, and high-rank service at enormous scale.

Solmere maintains pragmatic trade across both human and monster polities and is one of the human states most comfortable dealing openly with intelligent monster populations.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

11.content:
ILYRION

Position: south-central riverlands.
Capital: Sanctum Vale.
Status: major kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 1.

Identity:
Ilyrion is famous for temples, healers, soul rites, pilgrimage routes, and religious scholarship.
Many of Avereth's best-known resurrection specialists train or serve here.

The kingdom is not a theocracy, but temples possess major political and economic influence.

Several ancient faiths associated with historically famous S-rank figures or traditions maintain important sanctuaries in Ilyrion.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

12.content:
DUSKREACH

Position: southeastern marches.
Capital: Blackgate.
Status: regional human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: none.

Identity:
Duskreach is a hard frontier realm with strong B- and A-rank military figures but no known Full-Divine protector.

It survives through fortifications, alliances, Guild contracts, mercenary service, and careful diplomacy with stronger neighbors.

Its rulers are acutely aware that wealth and armies cannot fully substitute for an S-rank at the kingdom level.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

13.content:
ASHEN SCALE DOMINION

Position: volcanic eastern highlands.
Seat of power: the Cinder Throne.
Status: strongest recognized monster realm.
Public S-ranks: 3.

Identity:
The Dominion is ruled by ancient draconic and scaled bloodlines alongside other fire- and mountain-adapted monster species.

Its oldest rulers think in centuries rather than years.
Strength, bloodline, territory, oath, and personal authority matter more than human-style bureaucracy.

The Dominion is Veyrhold's most dangerous neighbor.
Neither side seeks a war large enough to force direct S-rank confrontation.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

14.content:
VERDANT FANG COURT

Position: ancient western forests.
Seat of power: Thornheart.
Status: top-tier monster realm.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
The Court is a loose but ancient polity of powerful beast lineages, transformed predators, forest spirits, and other intelligent woodland species.

It is called a Court because status is negotiated through territory, lineage, favors, challenges, and old pacts rather than a human-style crown.

Its relations with Caelreth include trade, magical research, territorial disputes, and occasional cooperation against shared threats.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

15.content:
CURRENCY / EVERYDAY ECONOMY
Common currency: 10 Copper = 1 Silver; 10 Silver = 1 Gold.
Coins are whole units; the current standard has no fractional Copper.

Legal trade may include Skill Stones, Gear, magical tools, monster/Dungeon materials, healing, transport, training, maps and information.
Prices are intentionally local/contextual rather than fixed in Lore.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

16.content:
NATURAL DUNGEONS
Natural Dungeons are persistent supernatural ecosystems/resource zones shaped by concentrated mana and other established local conditions.
They can contain unusual environments, rare materials, Skill Stones and exceptional Monsters.
They are physical/world locations, not temporary game instances that appear only for Alaric.
Exact Dungeon rules, layouts, ownership and local history remain open until established.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

17.content:
DEATH / RESURRECTION
Death is socially real.
Powerful temples or specialists can sometimes perform rare, extremely expensive soul-return rituals through high magic.
Resurrection is not routine medical care and ordinary people cannot assume access to it.
Exact limits, prices, eligibility and formulas remain undefined until relevant.

rpg_compile.note: trigger fields mirror the compiled WorldInfo entry

18.comment: [LORE] Medieval Material Culture, Communication, and Travel
18.content:
MATERIAL CULTURE
Avereth uses a Western-fantasy medieval material baseline alongside mana and high magic.
Ordinary life relies on handcraft, smithing, mills, farms, carts, horses, sailing ships, fortified settlements, markets, written records and similar pre-industrial institutions.
Mana and high magic can accomplish things mundane medieval technology cannot, but this has NOT created a modern or industrial technological society.

Do not assume modern/industrial infrastructure or devices such as electrical grids, telephones, computers, engines, railways, mass industrial manufacturing or firearms unless later canon explicitly establishes an exception.

COMMUNICATION
Ordinary people communicate at distance through letters, messengers, couriers and travelers.
Magical long-distance communication is possible through sufficiently powerful magic, institutions or artifacts, but it is uncommon and not universal everyday infrastructure available to ordinary people on demand.

TRAVEL
Ordinary travel is by foot, mount, wagon/carriage and ship as geography permits.
Long-distance travel takes meaningful in-world time; do not compress cities or kingdoms together merely for narrative convenience.
Teleportation or comparable magical transport may exist when explicitly established, but is never assumed to be ordinary public transportation.

rpg_lore.name: Custom Progression Fantasy RPG — World Lore
rpg_lore.scope: Slim setting foundations plus 6 human kingdoms and 2 monster realms; medieval Western-fantasy material culture; mana/high magic; native fauna are part of Avereth's Monster ecology.
design_notes: Western-fantasy medieval material baseline with mana/high magic; no modern/industrial technology is assumed.
Ordinary long-distance communication uses letters/messengers/couriers; magical long-distance communication exists but is uncommon and non-universal.
Ordinary travel uses foot, mounts, wagons/carriages and ships; magical teleportation is exceptional unless established.
Adventurers' Guild is neutral/transnational but does not replace governments, guards, courts, militaries or property law.
Monster classification is ecological/mechanical rather than a synonym for hostility; domesticated F-rank fauna can serve ordinary livestock/mount/pet roles.
Dungeon, resurrection and economy lore are separated into focused entries to reduce unnecessary simultaneous activation.
Undefined Moonfen Compact reference removed; ambiguous S-rank-faith/Tier-2/Guardian wording clarified.
Runtime lore triggers remain shallow so tracker vocabulary does not reactivate broad setting entries during Combat.
